chunks: One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Hijr is the house of Ismail, and therein is the grave of Hajar, and the grave of Ismail.
ai.seo_question: Where are the graves of Hajar and Ismail located according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the status of Al-Hijr as the domestic and burial site of Prophet Ismail (as) and his mother Hajar (as), establishing it as an integral part of the Sacred House. In Shia jurisprudence, this identification supports the view that Al-Hijr is considered part of the Kaaba for the purpose of prayer, distinguishing it from the open courtyard. The hadith underscores the sanctity of the family of Ibrahim (as) within the holiest site in Islam.

en.hubeali:
One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Al-Hijr is the house of Ismail<sup>as</sup>, and therein is the grave of Hajar<sup>as</sup>, and grave of Ismail<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from abu Bakr al- Hadramiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Isma‘il buried his mother in al-Hijr and built a wall of stones around it so that people may not walk on her grave.”
